@graph.description: Meaw and the coaches at our Chiang Mai camp explain wai kru ram muay: what it means, why fighters dance, and what to expect if you visit.

mainEntity.name: What does Wai Kru Ram Muay mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wai means respect, khru means teacher, ram means dance, and muay means boxing. Together, the phrase describes a fighter paying respect to their teacher, followed by a ritual dance.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Wai Kru and Ram Muay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wai kru is the respect-paying half: bowing, kneeling, acknowledging the teacher and lineage. Ram muay is the dance that follows, performed around the ring before the fight begins.

mainEntity.name: Why do Muay Thai fighters dance before a fight?

acceptedAnswer.text: The dance honors the people who taught them, and it settles the mind and body before the fight itself arrives.

mainEntity.name: Is the Wai Kru ritual religious?

acceptedAnswer.text: It includes a Buddhist salutation at each corner of the ring, but it isn't mandatory worship. Most camps, including Wildcat, frame it as respect toward teachers and lineage first.

mainEntity.name: Do all Muay Thai fighters have their own Ram Muay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Largely, yes. The dance passes down from a kru to their students rather than being standardized nationally, so movements and rhythm vary from one camp or region to the next.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to perform the Wai Kru as a beginner?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Beginners can simply watch at first. Many later learn a simplified version as part of normal training, at their own pace. ---
